title: Portfolio, registry and correspondence operations in ANDS Studio
walkthrough:
You open the Portfolio page. A top bar shows the "ANDS Studio · portfolio" brand plus a user chip and chips: "Help", "Dossier manager", "Registry", "Correspondence", "Guided journey →". Under the "Portfolio" heading, text reads "Every product dossier in your organisation — module progress, filing gate and fee status at a glance," and a smaller line notes every change is captured in the dossier's append-only audit trail. Three summary cards count "Dossiers", "Ready to file" and "Blocked". If any dossier has a deadline in the next 30 days (or already overdue), a rollup strip appears: "⏳ N dossiers with a deadline in the next 30 days", an "N overdue" chip, "soonest first", and per-dossier chips (ID · date · label · owner). Each dossier row shows its ID, title and submission type; an Owner / Client / Due column (a missing owner or client reads as "—", a missing due reads "none set"); a mini module tower; a gate chip ("Ready to file" or a count like "3/7 modules"); a fee chip ("Fee paid", "Fee waived", or "Fee due" with an amount — it does not appear until it resolves, so there is no placeholder flicker); sometimes a litigation clock like "⏱ NOA: 12d for brand to act" or "stay: Nd remaining"; collaboration chips ("👤 assignee · N open", and "⛔ blocked" when a task is past due); and links "Open →" and "Viewer". Each day-counter chip (and each Right-to-Sell chip on Registry) carries a provenance popover stating the anchor date, its source (ingested notice vs hand-keyed), calendar- or business-day basis, the counting rule with an HC / PM(NOC) citation, and a "computed — verify independently" note. An "Export client status report (CSV)" button downloads a spreadsheet that now includes owner, client and soonest due. With no data you see "No dossiers yet." and a link "Create one in the dossier manager →".

You navigate to the Registry page. Heading: "Product registry" with a "Register product +" button that toggles a form. Acronyms (DIN, NOC, Right to Sell) carry glossary tooltips. A persistent notice reads "Record only. Registering a product or changing its status here logs a record in your own workspace — it does not transmit or file anything with Health Canada." A "Right-to-Sell deadlines" strip lists per-product due dates (overdue ones say "OVERDUE"), each with its provenance popover. The "Annual notification checklist" is tracked on the registry service for the workspace and year, not only in your browser: a note explains each tick records who signed it and when and lands on the audit event stream, and under each ticked item a line reads "✓ signed by <email> · <timestamp> UTC".

The Correspondence page is headed "Correspondence & notices" and carries the same persistent "Record only" banner: ingesting a notice, serving an NOA or logging correspondence updates your tracking only; filing happens through the guided journey's transmit step (CESG). A "Dossier" field pre-fills with your first dossier; pressing "Open" reveals three panels. "Notice inbox": if no lifecycle exists you click "Start lifecycle"; otherwise you pick a notice type (SAL, SDN, SRL, NOC…), a date, an optional HC reference and subject, and click "Ingest <type>", under a line "Record only — this logs the notice you received… It does not file anything with Health Canada." "Correspondence hub" lists exchanges with direction chips and a "Log correspondence +" form. "Form V / NOA register" lets you "File Form V +", "Serve NOA" and "Record s.6 action", with live day-counters for the 45-day action window and 24-month stay.
